title: Why does this PySpark job fail when performing the final checkpoint?
question:
This is tested on Spark 3.5.6:

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = (
    SparkSession.builder
    .appName("reproduce_union_checkpoint_example")
    .config("spark.sql.caseSensitive","false")
    .getOrCreate()
)
spark.sparkContext.setCheckpointDir("/tmp/foo") 

df_1 = spark.createDataFrame([("a",)], schema=["foo"])
df_2 = df_1.where("Foo == 'a'").checkpoint() #NB!
df_2.printSchema() #this shows the name of the column as foo
df_union = df_1.unionByName(df_2)
df_union.explain(True)
df_union.show() #this works
df_union = df_union.checkpoint() #this fails
df_union.show()
  • If df_2 is not based on df_1, the job succeeds.
  • If df_2 is not unioned with df_1, the query succeeds.
  • If I omit either checkpoint(), the query succeeds.
  • If I don't make the mistake in where() and write "foo == 'a'", the query succeeds.
  • If I run it as shown, it prints the following:

answer:
df_2.queryExecution.optimizedPlan.constraints might be the culprit: Set(isnotnull(foo#9L), (Foo#9L = 0)). Notice the casing of the second constraint. When union tries to merge the plan constraints of the two dataframes, it no longer can adjust the name.

In Spark 3.3 it's different, checkpoint() doesn't preserve every constraint from the original plan: Iterable(isnotnull(foo#12L))
